saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Ορέστης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man of Tyana in Cappadocia, dragged to death behind a horse under the governor Maximus. It prints an apolytikion that names him, taken here. The year it gives is for the persecution and not for him — «Την περίοδο του Διοκλητιανού διωγμού (περί το 289 μ.Χ.)» — so no `dates` object is proposed on the strength of it. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Orest, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Orest (a common of a single martyr, with his name in it)

english.text: Thy martyr Orestes, O Lord, in his contest received from Thee, our God, the crown of incorruption; for having Thy power he overthrew the tormentors, and broke the powerless presumption of the demons. By his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Χριστὸν ὁμολογήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσεβούντων, εἰδωλομανίας τὸ θράσος καθεῖλες Ἀθλοφόρε, καὶ δόξης ἐγένου κοινωνός, ἀγῶνας πολυτρόπους ἐνεγκῶν διὰ τοῦτο σὲ Ὀρέστα ὡς νικητήν, τιμῶντες σοὶ ἐκβοῶμεν δόξα τῷ παρασχόντι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι διὰ σοῦ, πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντος — the only hymn on the page of «Άγιος Ορέστης», and it names him.

english.text: Having confessed Christ before the impious, you pulled down the insolence of the madness for idols, prize-winner, and became a sharer of glory, bearing contests of many kinds. And so, honouring you as victor, Orestes, we cry out to you: glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.
